findings.finding: Approach step 2 tells agents the compaction sweep 'must not be killed mid-sweep'. rebar already tells operators the opposite. When a blocked writer's LockTimeout names a compact-sweep holder, lock_owner renders the remedy 'safe to interrupt: terminating it loses no data — the events stay live and the next trigger re-folds them'. The plan does not mention this message. After the change, the doc and rebar's own runtime message would give conflicting advice about the same process.
findings.location: Approach step 2 (docs/orphaned-processes.md passage); Acceptance criterion 1 ("so it does not kill one mid-sweep")
scenarios: A writer hits LockTimeout. rebar says the sweep is safe to interrupt, but docs/orphaned-processes.md says it must not be killed mid-sweep, and the agent cannot tell which to follow.
A future editor 'fixes' one message to match the other without knowing why each was written.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'must not be killed mid-sweep' with wording that matches lock_owner: the sweep is optional housekeeping and interrupting it loses no data, so leave it to finish. If it must be stopped, send SIGTERM so the fold in progress completes and the end-of-run push still runs. Optionally add a guidance test that the doc's wording stays consistent with _INTERRUPTIBLE_REMEDIES['compact-sweep'].

findings.finding: The detector's "let it finish; SIGTERM only" note contradicts the only case where the label can ever appear. By default find_orphaned_load reports only PPID-1 records above 3600 CPU-seconds. A healthy worker that exits within about a minute is never reported, so every labelled worker has already burned more than a CPU-hour, which is the runaway case the plan itself calls "a real problem". Telling the operator to "let it finish" at that point is the wrong advice.
scenarios: A sweep stuck in a hot loop passes 1 CPU-hour. The report labels it 'let it finish', and the operator leaves a runaway worker holding the store lock indefinitely.
findings.suggested_fix: In step 3, change the note to: "rebar detached worker exceeding the CPU threshold: this is not normal; send SIGTERM (never SIGKILL) and file a bug with the command line." Keep 'let it finish' only in the AGENTS.md/docs guidance for workers seen at PPID 1 that are not hot.

If the docs passage says the sweep 'holds the store lock', it will describe lock behaviour that does not exist.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the stop guidance worker-specific: the sweep stops cleanly on SIGTERM at a ticket boundary; GC and async push have no SIGTERM handler, so say plainly that SIGTERM ends them immediately and they should be left to finish unless they are clearly hung.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/compact_trigger.py:171-193: install_stop_on_sigterm is installed only on the sweep path.
search for 'signal' in src/rebar/_snapshot/gc_trigger.py: (no matches). run_detached runs 'under the detached worker lock'.
Plan step 3 applies the "let it finish; SIGTERM only" note to any record matching "those three modules".
findings.finding: The plan gives one blanket "SIGTERM only" note for all three workers, but only the sweep handles SIGTERM. The sweep stops at a ticket boundary via install_stop_on_sigterm. The GC and async-push children have no handler, so SIGTERM kills them at once with Python's default action (no finally/cleanup). For those two, SIGTERM is no safer than SIGKILL, and the guidance would claim a safety property they don't have.
scenarios: An operator SIGTERMs a GC worker believing it will stop cleanly. It dies mid-janitor while holding the detached worker lock, which leaves a lock to be reclaimed as stale.
An async push gets SIGTERM mid-`git push` with no cleanup, which is the same outcome as SIGKILL.

findings.finding: The stop guidance in docs/orphaned-processes.md covers only the compaction sweep ('SIGTERM … ends the sweep at a ticket boundary'). The detector note, however, applies 'let it finish; SIGTERM only' to all three workers. The plan never states what SIGTERM does to snapshot GC or the async push. findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the AGENTS.md and doc recognition rule describe the full spawn_detached command shape (interpreter + `-c` + import of the module), consistent with the detector. Add a detector negative test for a command containing the exact module string outside that shape.
evidence: "how to recognise them (command line contains `import rebar._commands.compact_trigger`, `rebar._snapshot.gc_trigger` or `rebar._store.push`)"
"a command that merely mentions `rebar` in an argument are not"
findings.finding: The AGENTS.md recognition rule is a bare substring check ('command line contains … `rebar._snapshot.gc_trigger` or `rebar._store.push`'). That is looser than the detector, which is supposed to match the spawn_detached shape and reject a command that 'merely mentions rebar in an argument'. Under the AGENTS.md wording, an agent-started process that merely mentions a module string is exempt. Examples: `pytest -k rebar._store.push`, `grep -r rebar._snapshot.gc_trigger`, or an agent's own `python -c 'import rebar._store.push; …'` loop. The detector negative test also only covers 'mentions `rebar`', not 'mentions the exact module string outside the spawn shape'.
scenarios: An agent leaves a hung `pytest tests/... -k rebar._store.push` at PPID 1 and treats it as exempt under AGENTS.md, reintroducing the busy-loop class the rule exists for.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define one recognition signature taken from spawn_detached's stub (`-c` plus `import <module>; <module>.<func>(` for each of the three module/func pairs), use it in AGENTS.md, docs and is_rebar_detached_worker alike, and for the sweep point to its worker-lock stamp pid as the confirming identity check.
evidence: Plan step 1: "command line contains `import rebar._commands.compact_trigger`, `rebar._snapshot.gc_trigger` or `rebar._store.push`"
src/rebar/_proc.py:146-153: the real shape is `<python> -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[N]); import <module>; <module>.<func>(*sys.argv[1:N])" ...`
AGENTS.md:336: "`pgrep -f <pattern>` matches command-line TEXT, not identity."
findings.finding: The plan's recognition strings are inconsistent and too loose. Only the sweep uses the anchored `import rebar._commands.compact_trigger`. GC and push use bare substrings (`rebar._snapshot.gc_trigger`, `rebar._store.push`), so any process that mentions the module text matches: e.g. `pytest -k rebar._store.push`, an editor, or a `ps | grep rebar._store.push` pipeline. That defeats the plan's own negative test ("a command that merely mentions rebar in an argument") at the guidance level. AGENTS.md already warns that matching command-line text does not prove identity.
findings.location: Approach step 1 (AGENTS.md recognition strings) vs step 3 (is_rebar_detached_worker)
scenarios: An agent sees a PPID-1 process whose command line contains `rebar._store.push` as a pytest argument, treats it as an exempt rebar worker, and leaves a real leaked helper running.
The AGENTS.md recognition rule and the detector's matcher disagree, so an agent and the script classify the same process differently.
findings.suggested_fix: Recognise each worker by the fragment `import <module>; <module>.<func>(` with the exact pairs (rebar._commands.compact_trigger/run_detached_sweep, rebar._snapshot.gc_trigger/run_detached, rebar._store.push/push_tickets_branch), and require the command to start with a python executable followed by `-c`.

It is also unclear what is pinned: the AC says 'a spawn_detached caller's module', while Testing says 'module paths passed to spawn_detached'. These can differ, because the calling module need not be the worker module.
scenarios: The worker module is built from a variable or f-string, so a naive grep finds nothing and the test passes vacuously.
The executor pins the caller file (e.g. a CLI command module) rather than the worker module and names the wrong thing in the guidance.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the AC to 'A test fails if a module imported by a `spawn_detached` worker command is not named in the guidance'. Have the test AST-walk src/rebar for `spawn_detached` calls, extract the worker module from the command argument, assert the result is non-empty and at least three, then check each module appears in both files.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the default: a labelled rebar worker over threshold is still flagged with an unchanged exit status, and give the exact label substring the test asserts (e.g. 'rebar detached worker: let it finish; SIGTERM only').
evidence: "the report line labels it as a rebar detached worker with the \"let it finish; SIGTERM only\" note. It is still reported when over the CPU threshold"
"Read-only behaviour unchanged."
findings.finding: The report line for a recognised worker over the CPU threshold has no defined label text or format. The plan also does not say whether such a record still affects the script's exit status. The executor has to choose both.
scenarios: The executor makes labelled workers exit 0 (treated as exempt) while another reader expects a non-zero exit (runaway is real), and callers of the script behave inconsistently.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to step 3: 'Exit status is unchanged — a flagged rebar worker counts as flagged. The line is suffixed with "[rebar detached worker: let it finish; SIGTERM only]".'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Derive the detector-test fixtures from the actual command strings at the spawn sites (or a shared constant/helper they use), not hand-copied literals.
evidence: "a record with the real `spawn_detached` command line for each of the three entry points is recognised"
findings.finding: The detector tests use 'the real spawn_detached command line' for each entry point. The plan does not say whether these are hand-copied literals or are produced by the same code/argv builder the spawn sites use. Hand-copied fixtures can go stale and still pass.
scenarios: A spawn site changes its `-c` code (e.g. `from rebar._store import push`). The literal fixture still matches, and the detector stops recognising real workers in production.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Document the identification command with unlimited width (e.g. `ps -ww -o pid=,ppid=,command=`) and confirm the detector requests untruncated command output.
evidence: "how to identify each from `ps -o pid=,ppid=,command=`"
"Portability: string matching on `ps` output only"
findings.finding: The guidance tells agents to identify workers from `ps -o pid=,ppid=,command=`, and the detector parses ps output, but the plan never addresses command-column truncation. Long interpreter paths (e.g. a venv python) plus a `-c` program can push the `import rebar...` text past the display width, depending on platform and the ps width options.
scenarios: An agent runs the documented ps command in a narrow terminal, sees a truncated line without the module name, and treats the sweep as an ordinary orphan.
findings.suggested_fix: In docs/orphaned-processes.md and the AGENTS.md pointer, use `ps -ww -o pid=,ppid=,command=`. Note in step 3 that the detector's ps invocation must request unlimited width.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the exact detached argv/command line each of the three spawn sites produces (especially the async push). Make AGENTS.md, the doc and the detector match that real string. Align the AC and Testing on 'module passed to spawn_detached' vs 'caller's module'.
evidence: "command line contains `import rebar._commands.compact_trigger`, `rebar._snapshot.gc_trigger` or `rebar._store.push`"
"pinned against the module paths passed to `spawn_detached` in src/rebar" vs AC "a `spawn_detached` caller's module"
findings.finding: The plan assumes each detached worker's command line contains its module path. It lists recognition strings asymmetrically: `import rebar._commands.compact_trigger` with the `import ` prefix, but bare `rebar._snapshot.gc_trigger` and `rebar._store.push`. If push_tickets_branch detaches a `git push` argv directly rather than a `python -c 'import rebar._store.push…'` command, no `rebar._store.push` string appears in ps output. The documented identification and the detector would then never recognise the push worker. The AC also says 'a spawn_detached caller's module', while Testing pins 'the module paths passed to spawn_detached'. For a worker launched as a plain git command, those two can differ.
findings.location: Approach steps 1 and 3; Testing 'Guidance' bullet; AC 'A test fails if a `spawn_detached` caller's module is not named'
scenarios: The async push spawns `git push origin <tickets-branch>`. An agent sees it at PPID 1, finds no rebar module string, and kills it mid-push.
The detector labels compaction sweep and GC records but reports the push as an unlabeled orphan.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the guidance test discovers spawn_detached call sites and their module paths (e.g. AST scan of src/rebar). Make it assert the discovered set is non-empty and currently equals the three named modules, so extraction failure fails loudly.
evidence: "pinned against the module paths passed to `spawn_detached` in src/rebar, so a new spawn site without guidance fails the test"
No statement of how call sites and module paths are extracted, or of a non-empty/expected-count assertion.
findings.finding: The guidance-pinning test derives its expected set from 'the module paths passed to spawn_detached in src/rebar', but the extraction mechanism is unspecified. If extraction finds nothing, the test passes vacuously. That happens if a call site builds its argv through a variable, if spawn_detached is renamed, or if a helper wraps it. A new spawn site would then slip past the very check AC3 promises.
findings.location: Testing 'Guidance' bullet; AC 'A test fails if a `spawn_detached` caller's module is not named in the guidance.'
scenarios: A refactor routes all three sites through a wrapper. The scan finds zero spawn_detached callers and the test stays green while guidance drifts.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the test assert `discovered == {'rebar._commands.compact_trigger', 'rebar._snapshot.gc_trigger', 'rebar._store.push'}` (or `>=` that set and non-empty) before checking that each appears in AGENTS.md and docs/orphaned-processes.md.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Build the detector test's positive command lines from the same argv construction the spawn sites use (or a shared source of truth), not hand-typed literals, so a change to spawn_detached's command shape breaks the test.
evidence: "a record with the real `spawn_detached` command line for each of the three entry points is recognised"
"add `is_rebar_detached_worker(command)` matching the `spawn_detached` command shape"
findings.finding: The detector tests feed 'the real spawn_detached command line' into records, but the plan does not say where those strings come from. If they are hand-typed literals in the test, they lock in today's shape. If spawn_detached's argv later changes (interpreter flags, `-c` body, quoting), is_rebar_detached_worker stops matching real processes while the tests stay green. This is a self-authored oracle.
scenarios: spawn_detached gains a `-I` or `-X` flag or changes the import statement. Real workers go unlabeled, but the fixture literals still match and CI passes.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Have the AGENTS.md sentence bound the exemption: exempt while behaving normally; if one is flagged by check_orphaned_load.py or outlives its expected duration, stop it with SIGTERM per docs/orphaned-processes.md.
evidence: "rebar's own detached workers are exempt"
"It is still reported when over the CPU threshold, because a runaway worker is a real problem."
findings.finding: The plan keeps reporting over-threshold rebar workers because 'a runaway worker is a real problem'. But the AGENTS.md amendment states only that the workers are exempt, with recognition and a pointer. An agent reading only the mandatory rule would conclude it never needs to act on a rebar worker, even one at PPID 1 burning CPU or running far beyond its expected lifetime (the incident sweep finished within about a minute). The carve-out's boundary is not stated where the rule lives.
scenarios: A sweep wedged in a loop holds the store lock indefinitely. Agents see it, read 'exempt', and leave it, blocking later store writes.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the pin test as an AST scan of src/rebar for Call nodes named spawn_detached that fails if any call's first argument is not a string literal, asserts at least the three known modules are found, and checks each appears in both AGENTS.md and docs/orphaned-processes.md.
evidence: Plan: "pinned against the module paths passed to `spawn_detached` in src/rebar, so a new spawn site without guidance fails the test"
search 'spawn_detached' in src/rebar returns docstring/definition hits (_config_sources.py:64, _proc.py:124/138, compact_trigger.py:145/147) as well as the three real calls.
findings.finding: The plan doesn't say how the guidance pin test finds "the module paths passed to spawn_detached in src/rebar". A grep for string literals near `spawn_detached(` would also hit the definition in _proc.py and the docstring mentions (e.g. _config_sources.py:64, compact_trigger.py:147). It would also silently skip a future caller that passes the module as a variable or constant, and then the AC 'a test fails if a spawn_detached caller's module is not named' would not hold.
findings.location: Testing → Guidance bullet; AC 'A test fails if a spawn_detached caller's module is not named in the guidance'
scenarios: A new caller writes `spawn_detached(_WORKER_MODULE, ...)`. A literal-only scan never sees it, the pin test passes, and the new worker gets no guidance.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `ast.walk` over src/rebar/**/*.py, collect `Call` nodes whose func is the Name/Attribute `spawn_detached`, assert `isinstance(call.args[0], ast.Constant)` (fail otherwise), and compare the collected set with the modules named in both documents.

metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)
